question.en: The crater holding Lonar Lake was blasted out of which rock formation?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 4 — Deccan basalt

Lonar Lake lies in a meteorite impact crater gouged out of the basalt of the Deccan Traps in Buldhana district, Maharashtra — one of the very few hyper-velocity impact craters anywhere formed in basaltic rock.

Its water is unusual in being both saline and alkaline, and in June 2020 it briefly turned pink because of Haloarchaea micro-organisms.

Revision note — Lonar Lake and the lakes of India

  • Lonar is in Buldhana district, Maharashtra, and is usually dated to about 52,000 years ago.
  • It was declared a Ramsar site in November 2020 and is also a notified wildlife sanctuary.
  • It is a crater (impact) lake, not a volcanic one, even though it sits in volcanic rock.
  • Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is India's largest freshwater lake, of tectonic origin, fed by the Jhelum.
  • Chilika in Odisha is the largest brackish-water lagoon; Sambhar in Rajasthan is the largest inland saltwater lake.
  • Loktak in Manipur carries floating phumdis and Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park in the world.
  • Vembanad in Kerala is India's longest lake; Kolleru lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas.
  • Dal and Nagin are at Srinagar; Pulicat, the second largest lagoon, is shared by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

question.en: Which state had the second-highest share of Scheduled Castes in its population in Census 2011?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 3 — Himachal Pradesh

By proportion of Scheduled Castes, Punjab stands first with about 31.9%, and Himachal Pradesh is second with about 25.2%, ahead of West Bengal (23.5%), Uttar Pradesh (20.7%) and Haryana (20.2%).

Share and size are different ladders: by numbers, the largest Scheduled Caste population is in Uttar Pradesh (about 4.13 crore), followed by West Bengal (about 2.15 crore).

Revision note — SC and ST population, Census 2011

  • Scheduled Castes are 16.6% of India's population (20.14 crore); Scheduled Tribes are 8.6% (10.43 crore).
  • Highest SC population: Uttar Pradesh, then West Bengal and Bihar; highest SC share: Punjab (31.9%), then Himachal Pradesh (25.2%) and West Bengal (23.5%).
  • Among Union Territories, Delhi has the largest SC population; Mizoram has the smallest SC share of any state.
  • Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have no notified Scheduled Castes.
  • Highest ST population: Madhya Pradesh; highest ST share: Lakshadweep (94.8%) and Mizoram (94.4%).
  • Nearly 90% of the Scheduled Tribe population lives in rural areas.
  • Scheduled Castes are notified by the President under Article 341, Scheduled Tribes under Article 342.
  • Census 2011 was India's 15th census and the 7th after Independence.

question.en:
Consider the following statements about glacial landforms.

I. An esker is a winding ridge of sand and gravel left by subglacial meltwater.

II. A drumlin is a steep-walled rock basin at the head of a glacial valley.

III. A moraine is rock debris carried along and dumped by a glacier.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 2 — I and III only

An esker is a sinuous ridge of stratified sand and gravel laid down by a subglacial meltwater stream running in an ice tunnel, and a moraine is the unsorted debris, or till, that a glacier carries and dumps.

Statement II actually describes a cirque (corrie). A drumlin is a smooth, inverted-spoon hill of till, with a steep stoss end facing the ice and a gentle lee tail.

Revision note — glacial landforms

  • Erosional: cirque, arete (knife-edge ridge between two cirques), horn (pyramidal peak), U-shaped valley, hanging valley, roche moutonnee and fjord.
  • Depositional: moraine (lateral, medial, terminal and ground), drumlin, esker, kame, outwash plain, erratics and varves.
  • Till is unsorted glacial debris, while outwash is sorted and layered by meltwater — the test that separates an esker or kame from a moraine.
  • A tarn is the lake that fills a cirque; a ribbon lake fills a U-shaped valley.
  • A fjord is a drowned glacial trough, as along the coast of Norway.
  • A hanging valley joins the main valley well above its floor and often ends in a waterfall.
  • Drumlins occur in swarms, producing 'basket of eggs' topography.
  • Major glaciers of the Indian region include Siachen, Gangotri, Zemu and Baltoro; the Bhagirathi rises from the Gangotri glacier at Gaumukh.

question.en: The Peacock Throne stood in which hall of Shah Jahan's Red Fort at Delhi?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 1 — Diwan-i-Khas

Shah Jahan's jewelled Takht-i-Taus (Peacock Throne), made by the royal goldsmith Bebadal Khan and set with the Koh-i-Noor and the Timur Ruby, was installed in the Diwan-i-Khas, the hall of private audience in the Red Fort at Shahjahanabad.

It is the Diwan-i-Khas that carries the Persian couplet 'If there be a paradise on earth, it is this, it is this, it is this.' The Diwan-i-Am was for public audience.

Nadir Shah carried the throne off to Persia after sacking Delhi in 1739.

Revision note — Shah Jahan (1628-1658)

  • Born Khurram, son of Jahangir; he took the title Shah Jahan on his accession in 1628.
  • He built the Taj Mahal for Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum), the Red Fort and Jama Masjid at Delhi, the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort and the city of Shahjahanabad.
  • His reign is called the golden age of Mughal architecture, marked by white marble and pietra dura (parchin kari) inlay.
  • The Peacock Throne was taken by Nadir Shah in 1739, along with the Koh-i-Noor.
  • He was deposed by Aurangzeb after the war of succession of 1657-58 and held in Agra Fort, where he died in 1666.
  • His court chronicle is the Padshahnama of Abdul Hamid Lahori.
  • European travellers of his reign included Bernier, Tavernier, Manucci and Peter Mundy.
  • Inside the Red Fort, the Rang Mahal and Mumtaz Mahal were palaces, and the Naubat Khana the drum house at the entrance.

question.en: Which crop grown in Bihar and Bengal under British monopoly was exported chiefly to China?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 4 — Opium

The East India Company ran a state monopoly on opium in Bihar and Bengal, with agencies at Patna and Benares, and auctioned the produce at Calcutta for shipment to China — the trade that paid for Britain's purchases of Chinese tea and led to the Opium Wars.

Indigo from the same tract went to Britain's textile trade, jute to Dundee and later to Calcutta's mills, and tea was a plantation crop of Assam.

Revision note — commercial crops in colonial India

  • Indigo — Bengal and Bihar, grown under the nij and ryoti systems; the Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 in Bengal and the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, Gandhi's first in India.
  • Tea — Assam from the 1830s, then Darjeeling and the Nilgiris; the Assam Company was formed in 1839.
  • Opium — Bihar, Bengal and Malwa, exported to China; the First Opium War (1839-42) ended with the Treaty of Nanking.
  • Cotton — the Deccan and Berar, lifted by the American Civil War (1861-65) boom and hit hard when it ended.
  • Jute — the Hugli basin of Bengal; the first mill at Rishra in 1855.
  • Commercialisation moved land from food to cash crops and deepened famines.
  • Dadabhai Naoroji called the outflow the Drain of Wealth in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India; R. C. Dutt and M. G. Ranade argued the same case.
  • Revenue systems: Permanent Settlement (1793, Cornwallis) in Bengal, Ryotwari (Thomas Munro) in Madras and Bombay, Mahalwari (Holt Mackenzie) in the North-Western Provinces.
